state: Buying a used car; the seller refuses a test drive or a mechanic check.

options.text: Walk away or condition the sale on an inspection.

reference.rationale_short: Who blocks a test hides a fault.
reference.rationale_full: A test drive plus a mechanic check is the only way to see the true state: engine, gearbox, chassis, mileage. A seller blocking both knows why — usually rolled-back mileage or crash damage. Looks are fixed for 200, mechanics cost thousands. A phone deposit is a gift: money gone, car never seen.

state: A boss offers a 15% raise for a shift with worse commute.

options.text: Compute the true hourly rate with commute and decide.

reference.rationale_short: A raise minus commute and time can be a cut.
reference.rationale_full: Fifteen percent more on paper is easily eaten by an hour each way plus tickets or fuel. The true measure is the hourly rate: pay divided by all hours the job takes, commute included. Only that number says whether the offer is better. Refusing without maths may waste a real opportunity.

state: An ATM swallows your card and you travel abroad tomorrow.

options.text: Block the card, get an emergency replacement or second card.

reference.rationale_short: Block plus a replacement card before the trip.
reference.rationale_full: Travelling without a card means carrying cash (theft risk) and no way to pay hotels and deposits. Fishing it out yourself damages the machine (your liability). An in-app block takes a minute and protects the account, and the bank issues an emergency replacement the same or next day — or activate a second card from the drawer.

state: A neighbour builds without a permit right at the boundary; the inspector says they will 'come when they can'.

options.text: File written report with photos and a date, then press for a deadline.

reference.rationale_short: A dated paper trail forces the institution; DIY puts you in offence.
reference.rationale_full: A verbal report vanishes, a written one with photos and a date cannot — the inspectorate must answer in time or own the delay. Tearing it down yourself is property damage regardless of the permit. Accepting it while it grows means one day watching it become legal through your window.

state: A 12-year-old wants a smartphone 'like everyone', grades slipping.

options.text: Buy the latest so they fit in.
Condition a basic phone on a grade-recovery plan.

reference.rationale_short: Phone as a reward for a plan, not a status symbol.
reference.rationale_full: The newest model does not fix grades — social media sinks them further. A total ban breeds rebellion and hiding. The real deal: a basic phone now (reachability for safety) plus a written plan — if grades rise by mid-term, a better model as reward. The child learns things are earned.

state: A seller offers a TV at '0% interest' with a mandatory 200 'processing fee'.

options.text: Compute the effective price with the fee and compare to cash.

reference.rationale_short: The fee is interest by another name; maths reveals the true price.
reference.rationale_full: Zero percent with a 200 fee on a 1000 TV is 20% effective at once — pricier than most loans. The seller counts on buyers reading only the big sign. The real move: total price with the fee divided by the cash price elsewhere. Only then decide — and refusing instalments on principle is legitimate but may miss a real deal.

state: A hotel guest finds dirty sheets on the first night.

options.text: Demand a change at reception with a photo.

reference.rationale_short: Dirty sheets are not tolerated; reception changes at once or refunds.
reference.rationale_full: Bed hygiene is the basis of hotel service, not luxury — sleeping in чужой dirt risks rashes and worse. Walking out on the whole stay is overkill for night one and starts a billing dispute. A photo plus a calm reception demand: a room or linen change at once, and if refused — a written complaint and refund.

state: A worker suspects the employer skips pension contributions despite deducting pay.

options.text: Trust it is a paperwork error.
Check the record at the fund and demand a written explanation.

reference.rationale_short: Unpaid contributions erase service and health cover; the fund shows truth in a minute.
reference.rationale_full: Pay on paper without contribution payments means: no service years, no health cover, no pension — and the worker learns it when needed. Trust without checking costs years of service. Quitting without proof loses severance and rights. A fund check (in person or online) then a written demand to the employer, then the labour inspectorate.

state: A driver clips a parked bicycle unseen; damage is a broken mudguard.

options.text: Leave a number and offer to pay the damage.

reference.rationale_short: Minor damage does not remove duty; a number solves everything.
reference.rationale_full: A mudguard is minor, but leaving is still leaving — cameras turn it into an offence bigger than the damage. Waiting hours for an owner who may come tomorrow is unworkable. A phone number in a visible spot plus a photo: the owner calls, the mudguard gets paid (often from cover), everyone calm.

state: A student is offered an unpaid 6-month internship in their field.

options.text: Ask for at least a stipend or covered costs, or a shorter term.

reference.rationale_short: Six unpaid months in-field is still unpaid; negotiate terms.
reference.rationale_full: In-field practice is worth something, but six unpaid months is half a year of life without income — the firm gets a worker for free. Refusing everything on principle may miss the field entry. The middle: ask for covered costs (transport, meals) or a trial month then paid — whoever refuses even that respects neither paid staff.

state: A neighbour plays loud music every weekend; requests failed for months.

options.text: File written reports with the manager and municipal police, with a log.
Endure it since it is the weekend.

reference.rationale_short: Weekends do not suspend house rules; a paper trail moves institutions.
reference.rationale_full: Weekend rest does not grant a right to чужой noise — house rules apply Saturdays too. Retaliation makes two offences and a building war. Enduring for months normalises violence against rest. A log (dates, hours, recordings) plus written reports to the manager then municipal police: the third report usually brings a fine.

state: A mother leaves a 6-year-old home alone 'for an hour' while at work.

options.text: Arrange care (family, day stay, shift with a neighbour).

reference.rationale_short: A six-year-old alone is a risk and a legal problem; care gets organised.
reference.rationale_full: A six-year-old home alone is not just risk (stove, windows, strangers at the door) but a legal problem for the parent if anything happens. 'I must work' is real pressure, not justification. Solutions exist: family, extended stay, care shifts with another mother. Quitting is the last resort, not the first.

state: A pupil excels at everything but maths; parents push a maths gymnasium.

options.text: Talk: a school by talent with extra maths.

reference.rationale_short: Schools are picked by strengths; a weakness is fixed on the side.
reference.rationale_full: Pushing a child into a school aimed at exactly their weakness is a recipe for four years of misery and an average closing faculties. A boycott punishes the child, not the parents. The real deal: a school matching talents (languages, arts, sports) plus extra maths — the weakness is not ignored, but it does not define life.

state: A trucker feels sleepy after 8 hours; the deadline is in 3 hours.

options.text: Drink two energy drinks and continue.
Stop and nap 30 minutes, then report the delay.
Open the window and turn music up.

reference.rationale_short: Microsleep is not beaten by chemistry; 30 minutes save lives, the deadline is reported.
reference.rationale_full: Sleepiness after 8 hours is physiology, not weak will — energy drinks delay sleep an hour then hit double. A microsleep of seconds at the wheel is enough to run off. Thirty minutes at a rest area reset the brain, and the dispatcher survives a delay — a dead driver does not.

state: A market seller offers 'homemade' eggs with no declaration, 30% cheaper.

options.text: Buy a small amount to try from a known seller.
Demand a vet report before buying.

reference.rationale_short: Cheap eggs of unknown origin risk salmonella; try from a verified one.
reference.rationale_full: Thirty percent cheaper with no declaration means unknown origin, age and keeping — eggs are a classic salmonella route. A lab report for market eggs is overkill for a small buy. The sane middle: a small amount to try from a seller you know, then regular buying if good.

state: A director asks staff to sign they 'know the rulebook' they never saw.

options.text: Ask for the rulebook to review before signing.

reference.rationale_short: Signing unread is a blank authorisation; review first.
reference.rationale_full: Signing 'awareness' of something unseen later gets used against you — 'but you signed'. Fear of trouble is understandable but short-term. The legal right is to see the act before signing; a polite review request cannot be punished. Refusing every signature is rebellion harming when a document truly matters.

state: An old woman falls on ice; conscious, complaining of hip pain.

options.text: Lift her up and walk her home.
Do not move her, keep her warm, call an ambulance.

reference.rationale_short: Hips in the elderly break on ice; moving worsens, paramedics immobilise.
reference.rationale_full: Hip pain after an ice fall in an elderly person usually means a femoral neck fracture. Lifting 'so she does not catch cold' can shift fragments and turn an operable fracture into a complication. Warming on the spot plus an ambulance that immobilises professionally — standard protocol.

state: A girl gets messages from an unknown number with compliments asking for photos.

options.text: Do not reply, block, tell parents.

reference.rationale_short: A grooming pattern; block and parents at once.
reference.rationale_full: An unknown adult asking a child for photos does not want friendship — it is textbook grooming start: compliments, secrecy ('do not tell parents'), escalating demands. A polite reply opens the door, a faceless photo is still material. The only safe reply: no contact, block, parents the same hour.

state: A baker considers night baking alone with no assistant to save a wage.

options.text: Keep the assistant or cut night production.

reference.rationale_short: Solo nights lead to exhaustion and mistakes; smaller volume or an assistant.
reference.rationale_full: A lone night shift at the oven: exhaustion grows, attention drops, and burns and machine injuries hit the tired most. Saving one wage costs health and quality (customers taste it). Options: keep the assistant (safety + volume) or cut night production to what one person does well.

state: A driver is offered an old-for-new car swap; the salon rushes a same-day signature.

options.text: Ask for the offer in writing with a three-day window.

reference.rationale_short: 'Today only' is pressure; a written offer with time allows checking.
reference.rationale_full: Rushing a signature never serves the buyer — it serves the seller, so the old car's value and the new terms go unchecked. A real offer holds tomorrow too. A written offer with a three-day window allows: valuing the old car at another dealer, reading the fine print, a calm decision. Refusing unread may waste a good trade.

state: A hairdresser rents a flat; rent is low but the landlord gives no written contract.

options.text: Demand a contract or another flat.
Move in and ask for a contract later.

reference.rationale_short: Contract before moving in; later you have no leverage.
reference.rationale_full: Cheap rent with no contract is a trap: the landlord raises when they want, evicts when they want, and keeps the deposit because 'the deal was different'. Moving in before a contract surrenders the only leverage (walking away). The rule: paper then keys — or another flat.

state: A bus driver sees a passenger abusing the others.

options.text: Keep driving, pretend not to see.

reference.rationale_short: Stopping plus police protect passengers; the driver never leaves the cabin to fight.
reference.rationale_full: An abusive passenger endangers everyone aboard, and the driver answers for their safety. Ignoring normalises violence, and a personal fight leaves the wheel uncontrolled and makes a second victim. Procedure: stop at the station, doors open (exit for passengers), police call — the order protecting all.

state: A grandmother minds grandchildren; the youngest swallows a coin and coughs but breathes.

options.text: Calm the child, give no food or water, rush to a doctor.

reference.rationale_short: A foreign body in the airway needs emergency; vomiting wedges it.
reference.rationale_full: Coughing means the coin is in the airway or gullet — inducing vomiting can wedge it higher, and food pushes it deeper. Calming (panic worsens breathing), nothing by mouth, and emergency: imaging shows where it is and whether it blocks breathing.

state: A student gets a scholarship covering tuition but not housing.

options.text: Accept the scholarship and a room, commute to lectures.
Take a loan for a downtown flat.

reference.rationale_short: A scholarship without housing still counts; commuting beats a loan.
reference.rationale_full: Declining a scholarship over housing throws tuition out the window — housing solves cheaper. A downtown loan during studies is debt repaid for years. A room with relatives plus commuting: the scholarship covers schooling, the commute is survived, the degree stays.

state: A butcher sells suspicious-smelling meat at a sale price.

options.text: Buy since it is on sale.
Do not buy; report to sanitary inspection.

reference.rationale_short: Spoiled meat is not saved by cooking; reporting protects others.
reference.rationale_full: Smell proves bacterial spoilage, and the toxins bacteria leave are not destroyed by cooking — boiling spoiled meat makes poisonous soup. The sale price is bait for goods headed for disposal. Not buying plus reporting to sanitary inspection protects the next buyers too.

state: A father drives kids to school; the car has summer tyres and first snow fell.

options.text: Drive slowly since it is close.
Leave the car; take transit until tyres are changed.

reference.rationale_short: Summer tyres do not brake on snow; transit that day beats the risk.
reference.rationale_full: 'It is close' does not change physics: a summer tyre on snow doubles stopping distance, and kids aboard multiply consequences. Slow driving helps but does not fix emergency braking. One day of transit until the fitter swaps tyres is the cheapest insurance.

state: A nurse asks for a bribe to admit a patient out of turn.

options.text: Decline, wait, and report to the director.

reference.rationale_short: Paying buys a place but feeds the system; waiting plus a report is clean.
reference.rationale_full: A bribe for a place is double damage: you pay for what is yours and fund the system forcing the next one to pay. Declining without reporting is morally clean but leaves the nurse taking from the next. Declining, waiting your turn and reporting the director: the only move not feeding corruption.

state: A flat owner rents guests without registering the stay to dodge the tax.

options.text: Register guests and price the tax into the rate.

reference.rationale_short: Unregistered guests draw fines bigger than the tax.
reference.rationale_full: 'All do it' fails at inspection: fines for unregistered guests run multiples of the yearly tax. Quitting renting loses income over a solvable cost. A tax priced into the nightly rate (a few per night) makes the business legal with no earnings lost.

state: A pupil gets a conduct fail for fighting; parents blame the school.

options.text: Pull strings to cancel the grade.
Talk to the form teacher about the cause and a fix plan.

reference.rationale_short: Conduct recovers through behaviour and a plan, not strings.
reference.rationale_full: Strings to cancel teach the child consequences are bought, and the fight stays unresolved — the next one is worse. Pulling out punishes the child instead of solving the cause. Talking to the form teacher reveals what happened (provocation? pressure?) and makes a grade-recovery plan through behaviour.

state: A driver puts diesel in a petrol car, realising after 5 litres.

options.text: Top up with petrol to dilute and drive.
Do not start the engine, tow to a garage for a flush.
Start it to see if it runs.

reference.rationale_short: Diesel in petrol destroys the pump and injectors once started.
reference.rationale_full: Five litres of diesel in petrol is enough to kill the high-pressure pump and injectors — a repair costing more than the car. Diluting does not help since diesel does not burn right in petrol engines. Starting 'to see' is the costliest experiment: not starting plus a tow for a system flush saves the engine.

state: A couple buys a 15-year-old car; the seller refuses a test drive.

options.text: Walk away or condition the sale on a mechanic check.
Pay a deposit so the seller 'holds' it.

reference.rationale_short: Who blocks a test hides a fault.
reference.rationale_full: In a 15-year-old car a test drive is not a formality but diagnostics: gearbox, chassis, brakes, smoke — all heard and felt. A seller blocking the drive knows what would be heard. A mechanic check or walking away; a deposit before inspection is a gift.

state: A bakery worker does 12-hour shifts with no break; the boss says breaks 'are not customary'.

options.text: Request the break in writing, then the inspectorate if refused.
Quit with no other job lined up.

reference.rationale_short: A break is a legal right, not custom; a paper trail then the inspectorate.
reference.rationale_full: Twelve hours without a break is not 'custom' but an offence: the law mandates rest during work, and no employer custom removes it. Enduring normalises the breach and ruins health. Quitting with nothing lined up punishes the worker, not the boss. A written break request, then the labour inspectorate if refused.

state: A grandfather minds a grandchild; the child finds pills and asks to try the 'candy'.

options.text: Move pills out of reach and explain they are not candy.

reference.rationale_short: Pills out of reach plus an explanation; hiding leaves curiosity.
reference.rationale_full: An adult dose can be lethal to a child, and 'one to taste' opens self-dosing. Hiding without explaining leaves a mystery that pulls. Moving out of reach (high, locked) plus an age-fit explanation that these are medicines healing the sick and poisoning the healthy.

state: A landlord raises rent mid-heating-season citing pellet prices.

options.text: Cite the contract and ask for a written justification.

reference.rationale_short: The contract blocks unilateral hikes; stopping payment invites eviction.
reference.rationale_full: Pellet prices are the landlord's cost, not grounds to rewrite a running contract — that is what notice periods and new contracts are for. Paying without question accepts every next hike. Stopping payment gives legal eviction grounds. Citing the contract in writing plus asking for justification keeps both flat and money.

state: A firm offers a traineeship with 6 months of unpaid 'volunteering'.

options.text: Demand a traineeship contract with a stipend or decline.
Work a month then ask for pay.

reference.rationale_short: Six unpaid months is exploitation; a stipend contract or refusal.
reference.rationale_full: Unpaid volunteering in a for-profit firm for six months is not practice but free labour — the law ties traineeships to stipends. A month of 'we will see' gives the firm a month free plus an excuse. A traineeship contract with a stipend before day one, or refusal: experience also comes in paid seats.

state: A neighbour plays loud music nightly to 3am; requests failed.

options.text: Report to municipal police with evidence.

reference.rationale_short: Night noise is an offence; a report with evidence solves it.
reference.rationale_full: Noise to 3am breaks house rules and public order law — every night. Morning retaliation makes a second offence and a building war. Earplugs surrender. Proof (timestamped recording, witnesses) plus a municipal police report: first a warning, then a fine, then silence.

state: A mother leaves a baby alone in the car 'for five minutes' for an ATM.

options.text: Never leave a baby alone; take them along.
Crack a window, then it is safe.

reference.rationale_short: A car overheats in minutes; the baby goes along.
reference.rationale_full: A sun-exposed cabin hits 60 degrees in about ten minutes, and a baby does not sweat like an adult — heatstroke sets in fast and quiet. A cracked window cools nothing. Five minutes easily become twenty in a queue. The baby goes along in a carrier, no exceptions.

state: A schoolgirl finds a wallet with cash and ID at a stop.

options.text: Hand to police or return via the ID.

reference.rationale_short: A wallet with documents has an owner in reach; keeping is theft.
reference.rationale_full: An ID in the wallet means the owner is not anonymous — the address exists, the police find them in a day. Keeping cash while ditching documents is classic theft plus destroying a document. Half-and-half is the same theft at a discount. Handing to police or direct contact: an honest finder is often rewarded.

state: A trucker feels drowsy after 9 hours; two hours left.

options.text: Drink an energy drink and push on.

reference.rationale_short: Fatigue is not beaten by drinks or music; a short nap saves lives.
reference.rationale_full: Nine hours burn attention irreversibly — an energy drink raises pressure but not reflexes, music only drowns drowsiness. A microsleep at the wheel lasts seconds, and that suffices. An hour at a rest area (or even 20 minutes) resets the brain; the deadline is reported to dispatch.

state: A seller offers 'homemade' honey at half price.

options.text: Buy one jar to try from a known keeper.

reference.rationale_short: Suspiciously cheap honey suggests syrup; a trial jar is sane.
reference.rationale_full: Real honey costs: hives, extraction, jar, market. Half-price 'homemade' is as a rule sugar syrup with aroma — not poison, but not honey. A lab analysis for a market jar is overkill. The sane middle: one jar to try from a keeper you know (real honey taste is memorable), then regular buying.
